chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from some of his companions, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Mubārak, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Abī Jamīlah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a slave and a free man who killed a free man, he said: “If he wishes, he may kill the free man; and if he wishes, he may kill the slave. And if he chooses to kill the free man, he shall strike the two sides of the slave.”

key_terms.حُرٍّ: a free person; used for both the perpetrator and the victim in this report
key_terms.رَجُلًا حُرًّا: a free man; the person killed in the case under discussion
key_terms.ضَرَبَ جَنْبَيِ الْعَبْدِ: to strike the two sides of the slave; a punitive action mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: a slave; one of the two perpetrators in the ruling
key_terms.قَتَلَ الْحُرَّ: to execute the free perpetrator in retaliation
key_terms.قَتَلَ الْعَبْدَ: to execute the slave perpetrator in retaliation
key_terms.قَتَلَا: the two killed; indicating joint participation in the homicide

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave and a free man jointly kill a free man in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning retaliation in a case where a slave and a free man jointly kill a free man. It states the options available to the victim’s heir in choosing retribution, and specifies an additional punitive measure for the slave if the free man is executed.
